memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Make an altar of acacia wood for burning incense. It is to be square, a cubit long and a cubit wide, and two cubits high — its horns of one piece with it. Overlay the top and all the sides and the horns with pure gold, and make a gold molding around it." - Exodus 30:1-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A second altar is described here, quite different from the first. The bronze altar in the courtyard was for sacrifice; this smaller golden altar was for incense. One dealt with sin, the other with fragrance rising before God. And notice its position — inside the Holy Place, close to the curtain, near to God's presence.

Scripture itself tells us what the incense pictured. David prayed, "May my prayer be set before you like incense" (Ps 141:2), and John saw golden bowls of incense in heaven which are the prayers of God's people (Rev 5:8). The rising smoke was a picture of prayer ascending to God.

What a beautiful thought: God designed a dedicated place for prayer to rise, made of gold, standing in the holiest space available. Your prayers are not noise God tolerates. They are fragrance He receives. And note the order of the two altars — sacrifice first, then incense. It is because atonement has been made through Christ that our prayers now rise freely and acceptably before the Father.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I think of my prayers as pleasing fragrance to God, or as background noise?
How does knowing Christ opened the way change how I approach prayer?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that my prayers rise before You as pleasing fragrance because of Christ. Teach me to pray with confidence, knowing You genuinely receive what I bring. Amen.
